entities.summary: Bernardo the Japanese (died 1557), an early Japanese Christian convert and close disciple of Saint Francis Xavier, was the first Japanese person to set foot in Europe. Traveling to Portugal and Rome in the mid-16th century, he joined the Jesuits and met with Ignatius of Loyola, serving as a symbol of the potential for Catholicism in Japan before his death in Portugal.
